full_text_en:
Yumen Mou Processing Co., Ltd. v. Gansu Provincial Department of Natural Resources — dispute over mineral resource licensing

【Ruling Gist】

Since the illegality of administrative acts may, under certain conditions, be inherited, when an administrative agency makes several related administrative acts in succession, the People's Court may, based on the principle of comprehensive review, examine prior administrative acts from the perspective of evidentiary validity. Where a prior administrative act is illegal and sufficiently negates the legality of a subsequent administrative act, the subsequent administrative act shall be confirmed as illegal in accordance with the law, and a corresponding judgment shall be rendered, so as to substantively resolve the dispute.

Administrative Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Administrative Retrial No. 294

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yumen Mou Processing Co., Ltd. Domicile: Xinshi District, Yumen City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Lü.

Agent ad litem: Luo Yongxiu, lawyer at Gansu Zhengtianhe Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Gansu Provincial Department of Natural Resources. Domicile: Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Ding.

Agent ad litem: Yun.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Lei, lawyer at Beijing Deheng (Lanzhou) Law Firm.

Third Party in the Original Trial: Gansu Provincial Mou Metal Geological Exploration Bureau, Institute of Geological and Mineral Exploration and Development. Domicile: Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Wang.

The Applicant for Retrial, Yumen Mou Processing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "the Company"), filed an application with this Court for retrial against the Administrative Ruling (2021) Gan Xing Zhong No. 210 of the Gansu Provincial High People's Court, in a case concerning a lawsuit against the Gansu Provincial Department of Natural Resources over a mineral resource license. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review the case. The review has now been concluded.

The Company applied to this Court for retrial, requesting the revocation of the second-instance ruling. The main grounds were: 1. This case is an action seeking confirmation of the nullity of the administrative act of cancellation; the second instance's finding that the lawsuit was time-barred constituted an error in the application of law. 2. The second instance, on the grounds that "the effective civil judgment found that the former Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources had fault in the registration and renewal procedures, but did not find the cancellation act unlawful, and the Company failed to adduce evidence that the cancellation act was manifestly and grossly illegal," and thus determined that "the former Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources' cancellation of the Company's mineral exploration license did not constitute manifest and gross illegality," was also an error in the application of law.

This Court holds that Article 1 of the amended Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC provides that this Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purposes of ensuring the fair and timely trial of administrative cases by the People's Courts, resolving administrative disputes, protecting the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, and supervising the lawful exercise of administrative powers by administrative agencies. Accordingly, the trial of administrative cases should aim at substantively resolving disputes, timely resolving administrative disputes, and reducing the litigation burden on the parties. This case involves three administrative acts: the grant of an exploration right (registration and issuance of a certificate), the amendment (refusal to renew), and the withdrawal (cancellation by public notice). Since the illegality of administrative acts may, under certain conditions, be inherited, when an administrative agency makes several related administrative acts in succession, the People's Court may, based on the principle of comprehensive review, examine prior administrative acts from the perspective of evidentiary validity. Where a prior administrative act is illegal and sufficiently negates its evidentiary validity, the subsequent administrative act shall be confirmed as illegal in accordance with the law, so as to substantively resolve the dispute. Specifically in this case, the effective civil judgment of the Gansu Provincial High People's Court in (2020) Gan Min Zhong No. 603 found that the Gansu Provincial Department of Natural Resources had fault in the review process for the registration of the exploration right at issue, and that the refusal to renew the exploration right violated the principle of protection of reliance interests. On this basis, the Company filed the present lawsuit, requesting confirmation that the Gansu Provincial Department of Natural Resources' cancellation of the exploration right at issue was null and void. In this regard, because the cancellation of the exploration right is necessarily linked to the prior administrative acts — namely, the certificate issuance and the refusal to renew — when reviewing the challenged administrative act, the People's Court should consider the legality of the prior administrative acts together with the legality of the challenged act in a comprehensive review. The second instance, by ruling that the former Gansu Provincial Department of Land and Resources' act of publicly cancelling the exploration right at issue was independent of the prior registration and modification acts, and that the effective civil judgment found fault only in the registration and renewal procedures, but did not find the cancellation act unlawful, and on that basis dismissed the Company's lawsuit, committed an error in the application of law that should be corrected in accordance with the law.

In conclusion, the application for retrial by the Company falls under the circumstances provided for in Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Article 92, paragraph 2, of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 118, paragraph 2, of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

1. This case is hereby remanded to the Gansu Provincial High People's Court for retrial;

2. During the period of retrial, the enforcement of the original ruling is suspended.

Presiding Judge: Li Zhiming

Judge: Yan Wei

Judge: Zhou Mi

September 23, 2023

Judge Assistant: Yi Wang

Clerk: Wei Qiannan
